plan: Given my private value of $7, my goal is to win the item while ensuring the third-highest bid is low. Assuming others bid close to their values, I should bid slightly above my value to secure a win if their values are low. I will bid $8, expecting others might bid conservatively. This way, I maximize profit if the third-highest bid is lower than my value.

Given my value of $18, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize profit if I win. Assuming others bid close to their values, bidding $17.5 could win if their values are lower. If they bid higher, I lose but incur no cost. This strategy balances winning potential and profit maximization.

Given my value of $44, I aim to bid slightly below my value to maximize profit if I win. Assuming others bid near their value, I will bid $43. This may deter others from bidding higher, as they might not risk overbidding their value. If I win, I gain $44 minus the third-highest bid. If I lose, I lose nothing. This strategy balances risk and reward, considering there's only one round.
